provenance: Original synthetic miniature catalog, authored for this example. No real customer, vendor, live export, or external service is represented.

source.profile_evidence: This fixture export profile explicitly serialized the independently authored expected rows as Windows-1252, with comma delimiters, doubled ASCII quotes and CRLF record separators. This declaration applies only to the captured filename, byte size and SHA-256 above. It is a construction record, not an inference from readability or decoder acceptance.

consumer.name: Python standard-library csv.reader
consumer.field_types: all strings; no type inference or evaluation

output.newline_detail: Preserve every decoded CR and LF at its original character position, including quoted embedded CRLF. Do not reserialize CSV.

ambiguous.csv.history: Authored with raw C3 A9 in label. Deliberately no export profile or independent intended label is supplied. Both UTF-8 and Windows-1252 are plausible byte interpretations.
ambiguous.csv.next_request: Provide the export encoding tied to these bytes or the authoritative label for record 0040.

known-lossy-utf8.csv.history: Original synthetic loss experiment: name was saved after cp1252 bytes were incorrectly decoded as UTF-8 with replacement; title was saved after ASCII encoding with replacement. The record-specific pre-loss strings are not retained. The checker gives two distinct possible predecessors for each field, which yield the identical current text. The known history, not the mere presence of U+FFFD or ?, establishes the hold.
known-lossy-utf8.csv.next_request: Obtain an earlier original or authoritative replacement for both affected fields; keep the current file unchanged.

literal-unicode-utf8.csv.history: Authored directly as UTF-8 with intentional literal U+FFFD, an ordinary question mark, and interior U+FEFF between pre and post. There is no leading signature and no recorded lossy conversion. The interior U+FEFF is content under this fixture contract, not a removable signature.

limits: Fixture-specific rehearsal; changed inputs need their own provenance and contract.
The hashes tie checks to captured bytes, not authenticity.
Parser readback does not establish Excel import, service ingestion, glyph appearance, or real-world semantic correctness.
